plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and build cash.
Add to QQQI to increase income exposure.
Trim CRWD to 10% to reduce single name concentration.
Hold remaining cash for capital preservation.
conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration risk, aiming for lower drawdowns but also capping upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2%.
Trim SPY to 25% to address concentration and leverage.
Buy GGLL at 4% as a new, high-potential addition.
Trim CRWD to 10% to further diversify.
This blend aims for risk-first growth with a target of ~2.5% monthly.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets ~2.5% monthly return by reducing leverage and concentration while adding a promising new name. It seeks growth but prioritizes managing risk first, with a moderate cash buffer.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL to 6% each.
Buy GGLL at 6% to capitalize on its strong setup.
Add to CRWD, increasing its position to 10%.
Trim SPY to 20% to allow for concentration in favored names.
This aggressive plan aims for ~4% monthly but carries higher risk and drawdown potential.
aggressive.read: This aggressive strategy targets ~4% monthly by increasing leveraged ETF exposure and concentrating on high-scoring setups like GGLL and CRWD. Expect higher potential gains but also significantly larger drawdowns and amplified losses due to leverage and daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Significantly increase QQQI to 30% for income generation.
Trim SPY to 20% to free up capital for income assets.
Sell high-beta single names CRWD and SMH to reduce volatility.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions over growth, with a target of ~1% monthly.
income.read: This income-focused plan aims for ~1% monthly distributions by shifting heavily into QQQI and reducing volatile assets. While prioritizing lower drawdowns and reliable income, it's important to remember that distributions are not guaranteed and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
